scenario: A 68-year-old man has been on unfractionated heparin for 7 days. Platelets fell from 240,000 to 70,000 and a new foot clot appeared. He has no bleeding. A classmate starts warfarin alone and continues a low heparin flush.
question: What must be stopped, and why is warfarin alone unsafe right now?
options: Continue heparin flushes and start warfarin
Platelet transfusion as the main step, then resume heparin
Observation, because 70,000 is not low enough to matter
Aspirin instead of anticoagulation, because the clots are platelet clumps
Stop all heparin and anticoagulate with a thrombin inhibitor
correctAnswer: Stop all heparin and anticoagulate with a thrombin inhibitor
citation: Loscalzo J, Fauci AS, Kasper DL, Hauser SL, Longo DL, Jameson JL, eds. Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine. 21st ed. McGraw Hill; 2022.
examTakeaway: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia is an antibody against platelet factor 4. Stop all heparin and start a direct thrombin inhibitor. Do not start warfarin alone.
